scope: DXF Background object record identity remapping, allocation, binding and transactional retry.

source_context.schema: DXF group 5 is the object record identity; Background records inherit the common object identity while the IBL group's 340 secondary-Background reference has a separate target role.
source_context.implementation_gap: dxfRW::writeBackground emitted ent->handle verbatim and did not reserve or bind the record identity, so a source remap could change the secondary-reference target without changing the Background record's own identity.

implementation.behavior: A supplied source identity is remapped, checked against invalid and fixed output handles, reserved, emitted as group 5, and bound to the emitted object identity after successful record serialization. A zero/no-source identity is allocated before the record scope and emitted. RecordStateScope and DxfWriterRecordScope protect the identity map and record bytes.
implementation.reference_policy: The IBL group-340 reference retains resolver-first behavior with handle-remap fallback after its existing same-root target registration check; the resolver does not replace the remap for group-5 record identity.
implementation.failure_behavior: A late invalid EED value leaves the prior destination bytes unchanged and does not publish a source-object identity binding. A corrected fresh writer emits and binds the remapped identity.

validation.input: Generated in-memory Background records only; no DWG/DXF fixture was added.
controls: group-5 identity follows the source remap independently of IBL group-340 resolver/remap selection
no-source Background identity is allocated and read back
late invalid EED rolls back record bytes and leaves no source identity binding
corrected fresh-writer retry emits and binds the remapped group-5 identity

qualification_limits: Generated controls do not establish complete physical Background producer coverage or source graph closure.
No independent native consumer or lighting evaluation was used.
This transport fix does not promote Background support claims.
